title: What is best practice for training intensity and duration distribution in endurance athletes?
publisher: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
claims: Descriptive studies of nationally or internationally competitive endurance athletes training 10 to 13 times per week converge on a distribution in which about 80% of sessions are performed at low intensity (2 mM blood lactate).
About 20% of sessions are dominated by high-intensity work such as interval training at approximately 90% VO2max.
Training intensification studies in already well-trained athletes do not provide convincing evidence that greater emphasis on high-intensity interval training gives long-term performance gains.
The predominance of low-intensity, long-duration training combined with fewer highly intensive bouts may be complementary for adaptive signalling, technical mastery and acceptable stress.
